Economy & Markets
• Spirit Airlines ceased operations after a last-ditch White House rescue effort collapsed, ending 34 years of flying and putting roughly 17,000 jobs at risk.
• Tech remains a market driver: Apple’s upbeat guidance lifted shares even as it raised Mac Mini prices, while chip stocks rebounded after an April surge; investors are separating AI leaders from laggards.
• War-driven energy shocks are rippling through the real economy, with the US seeing the sharpest fuel-price spike in the G7, Kenya’s flower and tea exports hit by higher freight, and Libya’s oil output at a decade high amid price gains.
• Wall Street traders far outpaced European rivals on commodities-heavy swings; the FT urges Europe to bolster the euro’s reserve role as geopolitical risk reshapes capital flows.
Why it matters: A bifurcated market rally led by tech is colliding with war-related energy shocks and policy shifts, creating winners and losers across airlines, banks, and commodities while testing resilience in the US and Europe.

• A new US mobile network targeting Christians will enforce non‑overrideable content blocks on porn and some gender-related topics, drawing scrutiny from security experts.

• Cuba denounced fresh US sanctions as “collective punishment,” while Peru opened a probe into trafficking citizens to fight for Russia in Ukraine.
Why it matters: Legal, military, and diplomatic lines are blurring as Washington repositions forces, asserts executive war powers, and sharpens sanctions—moves that reverberate from Europe to Latin America.

• A rare, fatal amoebic infection case underscores how multiple modest risk factors can combine into deadly outcomes, a cautionary tale for clinicians.
Why it matters: Regulatory shifts and new approvals are redefining access to care, while rare-case science continues to refine clinical vigilance and treatment pathways.

New York’s Old Guard and New Guard take the stage among a soon-to-be-revealed lineup of other acts, including the stage debut of MIKE’s Band of the Century group that he performed with for his Tiny Desk Concert.Daniela Lalita Returns with Mura Masa Collab Cut and Self-Directed VideoFor the first time in four years, Daniela Lalita has dropped new music. The Peruvian, NYC-based musician has presented her first sonic offering since the release of her Trececerotres LP in 2022, returning in full effect with “Tiroteo,” complemented by a Mura Masa contribution and a self-directed video. Lalita’s main source of inspiration? Caterpillars. “I took inspiration from the way caterpillars liquefy inside their cocoon, turning into a nutrient-rich soup through digestive enzymes that break down their own tissue to rebuild into an entirely different insect,” she said in a press release. Iconic.Vince Staples’ Official Album AnnouncementAfter dropping off “Blackberry Marmalade” onto DSPs, Staples responded to the “CRYBABY” internet discourse – confirming that the red baseball hat in the music video did, in fact, confirm his next studio album and its release date. In the words of Staples himself, CRY BABY is confirmed to drop everywhere on June 5.Also, in the words of Vince himself: "As the world burns, I have decided to release this album. Thanks for listening."​​ Read more here.Edward Skeletrix and North West’s “Let’s Have Fun” Video Features our Favorite Underground CameosNorth has really stayed busy this week, showing out as a featured artist on one of the lead singles lifted from Edward Skeletrix’s new album, Body of Work. The video though is what takes the cake for this one, featuring a compilation of cameos from our favorite underground artists, including Sophia Stel, Feng, Baby Osama, and jackzebra.North West’s Debut EP Loading…North West has been serious about getting into her music bag. After stacking a selection of solid co-signs and production collaborations from the entire hip-hop spectrum – ranging from Ice Spice to Che, and FKA Twigs to skaiwater  –West is ready to make her first longform move. With her first solo single, “PIERCING ON MY HAND,” almost three months old now, the 12-year-old is taking it to the next level with her first-ever EP. Entitled N0rth4evr, the project is slated to drop this Friday, May 1, and spans six new tracks – “PIERCING ON MY HAND” not included. West produced all of it herself.The Styling In Lady Gaga and Doechii’s “Runway” Video Is Some of the Best We’ve Ever SeenIt was only right that two of the best-dressed musicians of the modern era handle the lead single for The Devil Wears Prada 2. Doechii and Lady Gaga’s “Runway” delivered on every single expectation – sonically alone. Now, the visual is here, and it only makes us love the track even more, in which the duo runs through countless designer outfits.Kith’s $1,600 Fender GuitarUnder its Kith Records creative umbrella, Kith presented the latest installation in its partnership with Fender: a custom Limited Player Stratocaster. The guitar runs for $1,600 USD. Read the full story here.Vince Staples Readies ReturnAbout two weeks back, Vince Staples sent out an email blast to fans updating them on his new private Discord server, creating the channel as a way to “improve the fan experience.” He didn’t share too much else in that initial message, aside from the ominous: “Stay tuned, because there will be both hijinks and shenanigans…. I will be back sooner than you think.”And indeed he was. Over the weekend, the rapper took to Instagram to share his first-ever studio single since he dropped Dark Times in May of 2024. Uploaded to streaming earlier this week, “Blackberry Marmalade” harkens back to Staples’ old sound, leaning into a guitar-heavy beat, and premiered alongside a striking Bradley J. Calder-co-directed music video.Fans clocked a “CRYBABY” red cap in the visual – resting on Staples’ car dashboard for all of thirty seconds at the start of the video – with “June 5th” etched on the side.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: S.Pellegrino Brings Authentic Conversations to the Table With Lewis Hamilton
Entertainment.text: S.Pellegrino is officially kicking off its latest global push, and this one centers on something a little more personal: the dinner table. With its new “Dinner Dialogues” campaign, the brand is reframing its iconic bottle as more than just a staple—now a conversation starter, featuring printed prompts designed to move things past surface-level talk and into something more meaningful. Bottles with prompts like “What Italian habit should the world adopt?”, “What food takes you home?” and “Be right or be liked?” are just some of the questions designed to spark a great roundtable discussion.At the center of it all is a headline-grabbing moment with an intimate, unscripted dinner with Lewis Hamilton and a few of his closest, longtime friends. Entertainment.title: Isaiah Rashad Returns After Five Years With an Instant Classic: 'IT'S BEEN AWFUL' Is Here
Entertainment.text: There are very few modern-era, "hip hop"-identifying musical artists with an audience as wide-ranging as Isaiah Rashad.After stepping away from the scene for almost five years, when Zay made his at-first ominous return to the spotlight at the end of March with a mere minute-and-a-half video clip with little to no details on a presumed new album, everyone was in the comments. From Top Dawg Entertainment labelmates like ScHoolboy Q, SiR, Alemeda, and Ab-Soul, to other artists across all genres – Jordan Ward, Lola Young, Eem Triplin, BLK ODYSSY, IDK, and 6LACK , to athletes Zeb Powell and Taylor Townshend, and even Hidden.NY and Apple Music, everyone had something to say about the sole sign of sonic life to come from the musician. A few hours later, Zay formally lifted the veil on the official album announcement, revealing that his third studio album, IT'S BEEN AWFUL, would be dropping in just a few weeks.Ever since that sheet of TDE's somewhat-leaked, somewhat-confirmed list of projects for 2024 began circulating on the internet back in January of 2024, fans have been fixated on the rapper's next release. While Zay dropping in 2024 turned out to be inaccurate (ditto 2025), the project – which marks the musician's most creatively singular yet sonically diverse – has finally transpired over two years later, and we can already say: it was worth every minute of the wait.The rapper kept us fed in the interim, though, kicking the expedited album rollout – from start to finish, just about a month-long – into high gear right from the jump with an immersive narrative world. Spearheaded mostly by Omar Jones, IT'S BEEN AWFUL's visual identity has been aesthetically dialed in from Day 1, introducing listeners to the universe in which IT'S BEEN AWFUL exists, one cameo, song snippet, and captivating video foray at a time. Across the project's 16-song lineup, SZA and Dominic Fike show out on "BOY IN RED" and "CAMERAS," respectively, with TDE affiliate producer Julian Sintonia contributing vocals to "DO I LOOK HIGH?," as well as offering his production hand to a myriad of the tracklist."It’s been a beautiful mess getting here," Zay wrote in a message shared to the press and later on to his personal socials, reflecting on what he feels to be his most introspective and true-to-self LP to date."Over the years, I’ve tried on a lot of hats and faces until I found the skin I was comfortable in. This album is a love letter to getting there; going beyond facades and falling in love with what kept me safe (da music) when I needed to pour myself into something for sanity. In doing so, I couldn’t escape my appreciation for you. The listener. The family. The vibers," he continued."From the people who helped put this together to the folks who jam my shit so much, y’all basically a street team (might be showing my age with that one), I love y’all. I pray the songs connect on that day you need ’em, like my favorite artists’ music would keep me together. Love y’all infinitely. ’Til the next time."1. THE NEW SUBLIME2. M.O.M3. SAME SH!T4. BOY IN RED (FEAT. SZA)5. SUPAFICIAL6. SCARED 2 LOOK DOWN7. HAPPY HOUR8. DO I LOOK HIGH? (FEAT. JULIAN SINTONIA)9. AIN’T GIVIN’ UP10. GTKY11. CAMERAS (FEAT. DOMINIC FIKE)12. ACT NORMAL13. 10 STATES AWAY14. NUTHIN 2 HIDE15. SUPERPWRS16. 719 FREESTYLEAnd now. The moment we've all been waiting for. Entertainment.title: "I’ll Be Back," This Time, in 4K: ‘Terminator 2’ Returns to Theaters for 35th Anniversary
Entertainment.text: SummaryJames Cameron's iconic science fiction action sequel is returning to select theaters worldwide for an eight-week runThe cinematic screenings will be available in original 35mm and 70mm prints alongside 4K and 3-D digital formatsThe release honors the film's groundbreaking special effects and Arnold Schwarzenegger's defining action performanceRialto Pictures and STUDIOCANAL are officially bringing James Cameron's Terminator 2: Judgment Day back to the big screen.For 35 years, the beloved film has stood as the architectural blueprint for the modern action blockbuster. Cementing Arnold Schwarzenegger’s career as a larger-than-life cinematic titan, the sequel set an unprecedented standard for science fiction, pairing groundbreaking computer-generated special effects with Brad Fiedel’s legendary electronic score. Now, drawing from its prestigious film collection, STUDIOCANAL and Rialto Pictures are translating that enduring cultural cachet back into physical theatrical spaces.The 35th-anniversary re-release is strictly defined by its granular screening specifications. To capture the massive scale of the cyborg killer's mission to protect Sarah Connor and her son in present-day 1995 Los Angeles, the film will be available across four distinct exhibition formats. Audiences can experience the milestone picture in its original 35mm and 70mm prints, alongside updated 4K DCP and 3-D DCP digital restorations. This comprehensive exhibition strategy ensures that the hyper-kinetic spectacle can be viewed exactly as it was intended, bridging the gap between 1990s action lore and premium modern projection.The 35th-anniversary screenings of Terminator 2: Judgment Day open in select theaters worldwide on May 22, including the IFC Center in New York, American Cinematheque in Los Angeles, and AFI Silver in DC, for a limited eight-week run.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Slawn and Opake’s “Super Toy” Pop-Up Doubles as a Hypebeast Magazine Celebration
Entertainment.text: SummarySlawn and Opake’s “Super Toy” pop-up lands in Los Angeles on May 9 (6 p.m. – 10 p.m.) at Secret Walls, featuring 350 hand-painted skate decks created collaboratively over the past few months.The one-night opening also celebrates their joint Hypebeast Magazine Issue 37 cover, marking the latest chapter in their ongoing, boundary-pushing partnership.London’s most disruptive pairing, Slawn and Opake, reunite once again, this time bringing their latest project stateside. Opening May 9 at Secret Walls with support from START Los Angeles and Spraying Bricks, “Super Toy” is a full-scale tribute to skate culture, anchored by 350 original, hand-painted skate decks created collaboratively over the past few months. "Slawn ran out of money and couldn't afford a skateboard anymore...so we painted 350," Opake tells Hypebeast. The show arrives shortly after the duo’s joint effort on one of three limited-edition covers for Hypebeast Magazine No. 37: The Architects Issue.Their creative dialogue has been building in public for some time. During last year’s Miami Art Week, the two staged Heroes, Villains and Violence at The Art of Hip Hop, while earlier projects like TABOO pushed at the boundaries of taste, censorship, and control. That same project saw Opake step in as guest editor for The Big Issue, designing the cover and sitting down with Slawn for a conversation that cut through labels, faith, addiction, and the value of breaking rules altogether.Speaking on their collaborative process for The Architects Issue, Opake frames it simply: “When it’s just me, I can spend hours obsessing over a single line. When I’m working with him, it becomes a conversation.” He continues, “He’ll do something that completely breaks the ‘rules’ I’ve set for myself. At first, I panic, but then I realize that’s where the energy is. The ‘mistakes’ are usually the most interesting part of the painting.”“Super Toy” opens May 9, from 6 p.m. to 10 p.m., with a launch event that doubles as a celebration of Hypebeast Magazine Issue 37. Copies will be available on-site while supplies last. Entertainment.title: Fashion’s Favorite Climbing-Inspired Sneaker Has an American-Built Update
Entertainment.text: The KEEN Jasper KM Lite has arrived with an American build that's both responsibly made and lightweight by design. First introduced in 2008 as the brand’s climbing-inspired outdoor sneaker, the Jasper now has a refreshed look that delivers sleek style without compromising on comfort or quality. Most noticeably, the uppers have been smoothed with discreet stitching while the heel counter is satisfyingly streamlined into the midsole. It’s a subtle shift, but one that quietly ushers the Jasper from trail staple to a pair that’s just as at home in the city as it is off-grid.For men, the Jasper KM comes in three versatile colorways: Canteen/Black; Khaki/Birch; Black/Steel Grey, while for women, colorways include Granite Green/Black; Cameo Rose/Black; Plaza Taupe/Bitch; Brindle/Birch. Furthermore, the women’s model will be joined by a Mary Jane-inspired variant, the Jasper KM Lite MJ. The dynamic lineup provides options that expand how the silhouette can be worn, from day-to-day utility to more styled, expressive looks.As a follow-up to the KEEN Made Classics collection unveiled in April, KEEN Made Originals arrives this May, dialing in on one of the brand’s most beloved silhouettes. With collaborative variants emerging from Engineered Garments, Hiking Patrol, 18 East and Gramicci in recent years, the Jasper has slowly but surely taken up a spot among gorpcore favourites, and it’s only getting better.While KEEN has been producing pairs in the US via its Oregon factory since 2009, the footwear label recently made a conscious decision to move to a new facility in Kentucky, granting it more robust distribution capabilities and — more importantly — expanding its responsible production initiatives. It was the opening of this new Kentucky hub that planted the seed for KEEN Made, a new sneaker line offering consciously sourced materials and forward-thinking construction not only for greater durability, comfort, but also a lighter environmental impact. With thoughtful specs, the Jasper KM Lite is far more than meets the eye. Each model coming from the new series features Trampoleen cushioning underfoot, KEEN.FUSION technology binding the sole and upper without harmful chemicals, and materials recommended by the Better Cotton Initiative and gold-rated LWG-certified tanneries. Together, it’s a build that signals a more considered approach to how the shoe is made and how it feels on foot.“Owning our own factories keeps us closer to what we love, consciously creating versatile footwear that lasts,” KEEN’s Senior VP of Product and Innovation, Scott Labbe, shared. “Here in our Kentucky factory, shoemaking is revived as an art form—by a community of local, talented workers dedicated to premium craftsmanship.”As the centerpiece of the KEEN Made Originals collection, the Jasper KM Lite is set for release on May 1 at keenfootwear.com, KEEN Garages, and select retailers.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: McLaren Golf's Debut, ALD's Return and Whim's Unplayable Green
Entertainment.text: This week, the crossover report taps into how different worlds choose to engage with the sport. Aimé Leon Dore returned to the golf course through vintage silhouettes and FootJoy craftsmanship, while McLaren translated automotive engineering into tour-level irons. Zara Home treated golf as something that can live inside the home, and Whim brought the sport into Milan Design Week as a stop on an art crawl.Aimé Leon Dore’s different take on the golf uniformAimé Leon Dore's latest golf capsule treats the course as an extension of wardrobe culture. Drawing from late '90s and early 2000s golf style, the collection reworks traditional silhouettes through relaxed fits, knitwear, shirting and an expanded FootJoy partnership. It turns familiar clubhouse references into something more wearable beyond the course.McLaren translates engineering into golfMcLaren Golf enters the space from the opposite direction to ALD: pure engineering. Their new irons series aren’t just a branding exercise either; they use the same logic found in their cars. By using Metal Injection Molding, carbon fiber and a structural mesh inspired by supercar frames, the clubs feel like high-performance machinery. It's a technical transfer from the track to the fairway. And specifically, in the bags of new ambassadors/investors Justin Rose, Michelle Wie West and Ian Poulter.Zara brings golf into the homeGolf showing up in Zara Home isn't the obvious crossover, which is probably why it generated a lot of online chatter. Rather than approaching the game through performance, it brings golf into the home through objects, accessories and small details that sit comfortably outside the course. Among the highlights, a $2300 USD golf bag is crafted in genuine bovine leather and Vice golf balls are stamped with the Zara Home golden emblems.Whim's unplayable green at Milan Design WeekWhim's La Cupola brings golf into design week as sculpture rather than sport. In the past, the brand has been known for building "Free Golf" pop-ups that people can actually play. This time, the concept shift into something intentionally unplayable: a dome-shaped putting green that suggests interaction but refuses it at the same time.From F1 to the fairway, Charles Leclerc tees it up with Rickie FowlerCharles Leclerc stepping onto the course with Rickie Fowler feels less like a formal crossover and more like a natural overlap. After all, this is the weekend when the Miami Grand Prix coincided with the PGA TOUR's Cadillac Championship. Coming from Formula 1, Leclerc brings a different kind of audience and energy into the game.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince’s ‘Helter Skelter’ Is Pure American Grit
Art & Culture.text: SummaryAmerican artists Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince will share the stage in Helter Skelter, an upcoming exhibition at Fondazione Prada’s Venetian venue, timed with the Venice BiennaleThe show brings the two artists together for the first time and will present over 50 works across photography, video, sculpture, installation and paintingA collaborative zine reflecting the artists’s creative exchange will also be on viewWhen we talk about appropriation art, Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince are some of the first figures to come to mind. Known for their visual riffs, both artists get at the edges of American popular culture, embracing all of its myths and perversions.With the Biennale around the corner, Fondazione Prada will present a duet showcase of work by Jafa and Prince at its Venetian palazzo. Curated by Nancy Spector, Helter Skelter is built around thematic overlaps and juxtapositions between both artists’s practice, such as authorship, race and image-making, threaded together by a shared concern for the contemporary visual landscape in all its good, bad and ugly.Over fifty works spanning photography, video, sculpture, installation and painting will be on view, alongside a collaboratively produced zine reflecting the pair’s creative exchange during the show’s development.“The term ‘Helter Skelter,’ reinvoked here as the title of this exhibition, contains all the complexity and messiness of its misuse in popular culture,” the foundation wrote. “It is an unruly readymade, selected by the artists to disrupt expectations, a perfect expression of the composite nature of this two-person show.”While working in similar modes, Jafa and Prince map distinct landscapes within American culture: Jafa’s work explores the intricacies and complexities of the Black experience, namely within music and film, while Prince’s practice mines a critique and fascination of white masculinity and the darker underbelly of national identity."They are both image scavengers,” Spector explained. “Seeking no prior permission, they dip into the overflowing reservoir of visual culture — from the swamps of social media to the annals of print journalism, from advertising’s hall of mirrors to Hollywood’s celluloid archive — to take whatever they want and convert it into art by choice alone.”“They are quintessentially American artists in subject and medium, literally enfolding objects and images from the empirical world into their works, subsuming them as readymades — Trojan horses, as it were, designed to disrupt established belief systems.”Helter Skelter will be on view at Fondazione Prada in Venice from May 9 through November 23.Fondazione Prada VeniceCalle Corner, 2215,30135 Venezia VE,ItalyClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Lexon and Jeff Koons’ ‘Balloon Dog’ Lineup Is the Perfect Harmony of Light and Sound
Art & Culture.text: For Jeff Koons fans looking to elevate their design game, Lexon’s got you covered. The French design house teamed up with the renowned artist for two functional art objects — the Balloon Dog Speaker and Lamp — reimagining the iconic pop sculptures introduced in the artist’s Celebration series.The new Chromatic Collection brings a techno-skeletal cool to Koons’ signature figure, delivering a rich experience of light and sound in four new limited-edition colorways for 2026. An up from last year’s lineup, the current collection introduces vibrant metal accents, while staying true to its signature transparency.If sculptural lighting is up your alley, the Balloon Dog Lamp brings on a futuristic luminescence, now in gold, blue, red and platinum editions. Equipped with a 9-color range, dynamic animations and effects the piece is geared up to set any mood. With the help of Lexon’s Easy Sync tech, the wireless piece can link up with other lamps, making for a perfect, synchronized ambiance.If you’re more of an artful audiophile, the collaborative speaker makes for the perfect addition. Arriving in gold, blue, red and white, the piece trades the dog’s original metallic sheen for a clear shell to show off colorful hardware. A hi-fi delight for the eyes and ears, the piece adds a balanced 360° ambiance and major shelf appeal to any space.“With the Chromatic Collection, we wanted to push the dialogue between art and design even further,” expressed Lexon’s CEO, Boris Brault, “adding color is a way to bring some emotion and joie de vivre to these special objects that live with you every day.”The new Lexon x Jeff Koons pieces level up from last year’s editions, with new strides in material innovation, acoustic calibration and LED diffusion, for a satisfying harmony of finish, tone and texture.Both priced at $800 USD, both pieces stand at around 11 inches tall and weigh in at 1 kilogram, arriving with a holographic certificate of authenticity and packaging, alongside the artist’s signature engraved on the front paw. The Jeff Koons x Lexon lamp and speaker is now globally available for pre-order via the brand’s site.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Lauren Halsey Readies a Technicolor Hollywood Bowl Takeover
Art & Culture.text: SummaryAmerican artist Lauren Halsey will open emajendat at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles on September 29The event will feature new works, technicolor staged designed by the artist, community activations and a concert to close it outLauren Halsey is set to take over the LA’s Hollywood Bowl come fall, transforming 18,000-seater in emajendat. Slated for September 29, the site-specific installation will include new artworks, community-first programming and a concert featuring the likes of Erykah Badu, Anderson .Paak, the Charles Gaines Collective and Black Nile.The campus-wide takeover takes titular cues from Halsey's 2024 presentation at London's Serpentine Galleries, which brought a slice of South Central LA’s backyard culture to London: life-size vignettes of community heroes, prismatic CD flooring and a trove of figurines, “funkmounds” and sculptures. While bearing the same name, the artist promises that the ideas and work included in the upcoming LA presentation will be “very new.”Airbrush stations, mini golf, ping pong and a roller “palace” are on deck for concertgoers with a special performance by Badu, .Paak (as DJ Pee .Wee) and more to close out the night. The concert will be held on a staged graced and designed by Halsey’s maximalist, technicolor signature.For now, further details are under wraps, though a press statement teases it will be an imaginative crossover between architecture, art and sport, fused with the emblematic civic urgency of Halsey’s recently debuted “sister dreamer” sculpture garden.Tickets for emajendat go live at 10AM PST on May 5 on Hollywood Bowl’s website.
